messages.subject: measurement invariance for dependent groups and two factors
parts:
Hi,
I want to evaluate measurement invariance for gender. The data is from a questionair with 10 items and two factors (so I can´t use longInvariance() ) and filled out from husband and wife (dyiadic data). So the groups I want to test invariance are dependet. The items are answered on a 6-point scale, so I think it can be treated as continous data?
Has someone information how to do this/how to specify the models?
Thanks for your help 
Kathrin

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: measurement invariance for dependent groups and two factors
parts: The items are answered on a 6-point scale, so I think it can be treated as continous data?

Well, Rhemtulla et al. (2012) indicated that with 5 categories or more, factor correlations are well estimated when treating the data as continuous, but that is not always the case with factor loadings.  You should also take into account how symmetric your thresholds are (click this link to read the suggestions in the article).

If you treat the data as categorical, you can read about how to do so for multiple groups at this link (including lavaan syntax examples).  Instead of making the constraints across groups, you make constraints across factors in the same 1-group model.  The same way that methods for testing invariance between Groups 1 and 2 generalize to testing invariance between the same factor(s) measured at Times 1 and 2, you simply have the same factor(s) measured for husbands and wives.
Has someone information how to do this/how to specify the models?

It sounds like you already provided enough information to specify your models.  Can you ask a more specific question?  If you need to know lavaan syntax, you can read the tutorial pages and the article.  If you want to know more about specifying models to test "longitudinal" (in your case, dyadic) measurement invariance, you can search the archives at SEMNET or even post your question there.

Terry

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: measurement invariance for dependent groups and two factors
parts:
Your syntax looks good, but a couple notes:
  • Husbands and wives are completing the same items, so the items correlate for 2 reason: (1) the common factors and (2) the item-specific factors.  In your current models, the common-factor correlations posm~~posw and negm~~negw will be overestimated.  In line with longitudinal factor models, you want to also estimate the residual covariances of the same items filled out by each member of the dyad (e.g., 'm1 ~~ w1', 'm2 ~~ w2', ..., 'm10 ~~ w10').
  • I'm not sure whether you have any missing data, but that is common enough that I'll bring it up just in case.  MLM corrects SEs and test statistics for nonnormality, but only works for complete data.  MLR is asymptotically equivalent but more general, allowing you to use it in conjunction with FIML if you have ignorable missing data.
Terry
